items.title: Live: Nifty, Sensex fall 2% this week; All eyes on Aug US CPI data | Closing Bell
items.description: The Nifty is set for its fifth straight weekly fall, with the Sensex down around 100 points and the Nifty trading below 23,400. Market breadth remained weak, while the India VIX jumped 4%, signalling heightened volatility. The Realty index emerged as the worst-performing sector, while metal and auto stocks remained under pressure. India’s 10-year bond yield crossed the 7% mark, touching a three-month high. Among Nifty 50 stocks, DRL, HCL Tech and Tech Mahindra were the top gainers, while JSW Steel, Hindalco and Tata Steel were among the biggest losers. US futures edged higher ahead of the August CPI data, even as the Dow is set for a 2.5% weekly decline and the Nasdaq is down around 2% for the week. The US 10-year Treasury yield climbed to its highest level since October 2023. Asian markets remained weak, with the Nikkei, Kospi and Hang Seng declining 0.6-2%. All eyes are now on the US CPI data, with estimates pointing to a 0.4% month-on-month rise. Oil prices are set to end the week above $100 a barrel for the first time in four months, with Brent crude cooling to around $106 after touching $109. Meanwhile, Houthi rebels have seized control of Yemen’s Port of Mocha, while Gulf shipping traffic faces restrictions following tanker attacks, adding to concerns over global oil supplies.

items.title: IPO STREET: RENTOMOJO, ARCIL, MANIPAL PAYMENTS & KARAMTARA — DECODED BY MONEYCONTROL RESEARCH
items.description: India's IPO market is witnessing intense action, with 81 companies having already raised over Rs 83,000 crore by going public so far this year, a number set to grow further with NSE set to launch its much-awaited public issue next week. The week of September 7 to 11 saw frenzied primary market activity, with as many as 12 IPOs launched over the past five days, four of which are still open for subscription. On today's IPO Street, we take stock of these four companies gearing up to begin their listed market journey. In focus is Rentomojo, a well-known furniture and appliance rental solutions company; ARCIL, or Asset Reconstruction Company of India Limited, a financial giant that looks to generate returns by turning around distressed and bad loan assets; Manipal Payments and Identity Solutions, a Manipal Group company that manufactures debit and credit cards, offers secure payment solutions, and also operates in the government ID ecosystem, producing documents like voter cards and driving licenses; and Karamtara Engineering, a niche engineering company manufacturing key products and components for the power transmission and renewable energy sectors. To make sense of these four new listings, Moneycontrol's research team joins the show to break down the issue details, business fundamentals, financials and valuation, and their view on each offering.
